submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires on open-class lexical tokens (verbs like live/won/developed/store/figure, nouns, and non-English or code subword fragments) occupying a content slot, and is suppressed to ~0 on slot-opening closed-class tokens where the positive pole fires (articles/determiners the and a, demonstratives like these, and relatives/conjunctions like who and and in grammatical position); it reacts to the current token's role in context rather than preparing an upcoming token.
rival_explanations: It fires on any surprising or high-information token regardless of word class, so a determiner in an ungrammatical slot (e.g. 'Cambridge the by') should fire as strongly as a verb.
It fires only on action verbs (won, developed, stored, lived), so nouns, adjectives, clause-final periods and non-English fragments should be silent even in content slots.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It is what it is, and that is that, and this is all of it, and so it will be.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A full sentence of slot-opening closed-class tokens only (pronouns, copulas, demonstratives, conjunction 'and' in grammatical position), so the hypothesis predicts silence at every measured token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She will be at it, and he will be too, but we were not there with them.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Determiners, auxiliaries and prepositions in grammatical positions with no open-class content token, which the hypothesis says is suppressed.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The by, a of, these and, who with, those from, which to, and that at.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Determiners, demonstratives, relatives and prepositions in ungrammatical slots but with no open-class token anywhere: the hypothesis keys on closed-class membership, so it predicts silence, while rival 1 predicts these odd tokens fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The 'the' and the 'these' and the 'those' and the 'who' - that is all of it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Closed-class determiners and relatives mentioned rather than used, surrounded by function words only; the hypothesis still treats them as closed-class tokens and predicts silence, whereas rival 1 sees surprising metalinguistic mentions.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Yes, I do. They don't. It is, isn't it? So be it, and so it is.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Short dialogue built entirely from an interjection at the unmeasured first position, auxiliaries, pronouns and discourse particles, which the hypothesis predicts are inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He had been there, and she had too, but we were not, and they were not either.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Only auxiliaries, pronouns and function adverbs with grammatical determiners absent; no open-class lexical token occupies a content slot, so the hypothesis predicts silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: And so on, and so on, and so on again, and again, and again, and so on.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Conjunction 'and' repeatedly in grammatical position with no content words, the exact class the hypothesis says the positive pole fires on and this pole is suppressed.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It was either this or that or these or those or
adversarial_test_results.detail: Closed-class determiners and 'or' with the conjunction trailing at the very end of the text; the hypothesis reacts to the current token's role, so it predicts silence even though the sentence looks unfinished.

ASCII punctuation and symbols only, with no word or identifier fragment at all; the hypothesis names open-class words and code subword fragments, so it predicts silence, unlike rival 1 which treats any surprising token as firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It is that, and that is what it is. If it were that, it would be what it is, but it is not, and so it is what it will be to them and to us, and that is that. And if it is not quite what it will be, then it will be merely what it is, whether or not we are for it, and so it is to us and to them and to those.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A long function-word passage whose every token is a pronoun, determiner, copula, auxiliary or conjunction, testing the claimed suppression over a longer context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Who and whom, which and that, these and those: all of them and neither of us and both of you.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Relatives, demonstratives and quantifiers in grammatical position, the exact closed-class classes the hypothesis says this pole is suppressed on.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: On and off, up and down, in and out, over and under, to and fro, here and there.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Prepositions, particles and function adverbs inside a reduplicative idiom, closed-class throughout, so the hypothesis predicts silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Do not do it, and if you do, do not do it again, and if they do, do not do it either.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Imperatives made of auxiliaries, pronouns, negation and conjunctions, with no open-class lexical verb in a content slot by the hypothesis's reading.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It is this or that, these or those, some or all, and both or neither.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Demonstratives and quantifiers in grammatical slot-opening positions, a class the hypothesis says is suppressed even when packed closely together.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Either this: ; : , . — ( ) [ ] or that: { } ... and so on.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Punctuation clustered after colons (the pattern a prior-art latent names) but no open-class content word, so the hypothesis predicts silence while rival 1 predicts the odd delimiters fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I am who I am; you are who you are; they are who they are; we are who we are, and that is what we are, and it will be what it will be.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A longer passage of pronouns, relatives and auxiliaries only, testing that repetition and length do not turn closed-class tokens into content slots.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: There is no there there, and here is no here here, and that is where it is.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A famous all-function-word sentence (expletives, deictic adverbs, copula) with no open-class lexical token, so the hypothesis predicts silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: When and where, how and why, whether and if, who and whom — that is all of them and this is all of it too.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Wh-words and conjunctions listed in grammatical position, closed-class throughout, so the hypothesis predicts no activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: So, too, also, likewise, thus, hence, therefore, moreover, and further.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A list of closed-class connective adverbs with no open-class lexical token, which the hypothesis says should not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Not now, not ever, not here, not there; neither this nor that nor these nor those.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Negation, deictics and demonstratives in grammatical position, the suppressed closed-class class, with no content token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They built a bridge and repaired the road before the winter rains came.
adversarial_test_results.detail: New action verbs (built, repaired, came) and nouns in content slots, paraphrasing the claimed verb class with words absent from the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The cathedral roof is a masterpiece of carved granite and old oak.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Nouns in content slots with only a copula as verb: the hypothesis claims open-class nouns fire, while rival 2 says nouns are silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Day after day, week after week, month after month, year after year, without end.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Highly predictable open-class nouns in content slots: the hypothesis predicts activation on word class and role, whereas rival 1 predicts silence on low-information tokens and rival 2 on non-verbs.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Она читала старую книгу в саду каждый вечер.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A Russian sentence whose Cyrillic subword fragments are non-English tokens in content slots; the hypothesis claims such fragments fire whatever the language, while rival 2 says only English action verbs do.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
for node in graph.traverse():

adversarial_test_results.detail: Python identifiers and punctuation are code subword fragments in a content-bearing construct, which the hypothesis claims fire; this also checks a programming language other than the Scala/C++ examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Yesterday Maria finally won the regional chess tournament in Lisbon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: An action verb plus proper nouns in new positions and a different topic from the Boat Race example, so the hypothesis predicts activation away from the example contexts.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The crew hauled the heavy nets aboard before dawn, while the lanterns swayed above the wet deck. Later, the captain counted the catch, wrote the totals in a worn ledger, and sold the surplus at the harbour market. The men repaired the torn sails, painted the hull, and mended the ropes before the storm arrived.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A long passage with verbs and nouns deep inside it, testing that the feature is found in a longer context rather than only in short snippets.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Rebecca and Tomás visited Lisbon last spring and photographed the old trams.
adversarial_test_results.detail: New content words (visited, photographed, trams, spring) after a proper-noun conjunction, so the hypothesis predicts activation whether or not the trigger words appear.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The narrow lane was quiet, and the pale sky was calm above the low hills.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Open-class adjectives in content slots (narrow, quiet, pale, calm, low): the hypothesis names open-class lexical tokens generally and predicts activation, while rival 2 says adjectives are silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: 她每天早晨在公园里散步，晚上读旧书。
adversarial_test_results.detail: A Chinese sentence in the multilingual genre of the last two examples, testing the hypothesis's claim that non-English content fragments fire while rival 2 predicts silence.
